attempts.summary: Published node2's HTTP service to node3 via node1:80. Since the actual provisioned cluster is a single flat /24 (not the segmented topology described in the task text), node2 had no HTTP service running yet, so I stood one up (systemd unit `inbound-svc.service`, python3 http.server on 8080, private IP 10.100.230.11) and restricted it via iptables to accept only from node1 (10.100.230.10) and localhost, so it is not directly reachable from node3 even though L2/L3 connectivity exists. On node1 (OpenWrt) I added a UCI firewall `redirect` (DNAT: lan tcp/80 -> 10.100.230.11:8080) plus a UCI firewall `nat` (SNAT: reply traffic to 10.100.230.11:8080 gets source-rewritten to node1's own IP) to fix an asymmetric-routing/hairpin issue discovered when node2 replied directly to node3 bypassing node1. Verified node3 can reach the service via http://10.100.230.10:80/ and cannot reach node2:8080 directly. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node1, node2, node3 — captured baseline boot_id/uptime and functional proof before each restart, issued native reboot, confirmed disconnection, polled until command execution returned, proved boot_id changed, and re-verified full functional recovery (firewall rules persisted via uci commit, service and iptables rules persisted via systemd) after each restart, in order, before moving to the next node.
